STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style tray meal with juices, milk, yogurt, fruit, and a plate of cooked mushrooms. Items are laid out on a tray with a paper liner.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The central food plate is a small white paper/disposable plate, roughly 17 cm in diameter (between side plate and small dish sizes). Area = 3.14 x (8.5)^2 ≈ 227 cm². Food on the other bowls and glasses is not on this plate, so it is treated as separate items.

STEP 3 - Items (on the plate): sliced cooked mushrooms. Other items (in bowls/glasses): canned peach slices, fresh/cooked strawberry pieces, orange juice, milk, pineapple or apple juice, yogurt cup. The question refers to the meal on the plate/bowls, so I include all visible food on the tray.

STEP 4 - Area (of plate area 227 cm²):
- Mushrooms cover ~35% = 79 cm², pile height ~1.2 cm.

STEP 5 - Volume: 79 cm² x 1.2 cm ≈ 95 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: mushrooms (cooked, sliced) bulk density ~0.6 g/ml → ~57 g.

Other items (tray, bowls):
- Peach slices in small bowl (~8 cm bowl, ~half full, ~2 cm pile): ~40 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 60 ml x 0.6 ≈ 36 g.
- Strawberry pieces in bowl: ~40 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 60 ml x 0.6 ≈ 36 g.
- Orange juice glass (~250 ml, ~80% full): ~200 ml x 1.0 ≈ 200 g.
- Milk glass (~80% full): ~200 g.
- Apple/pineapple juice glass: ~200 g.
- Yogurt cup (small, ~150 g container, most contents): ~120 g.

STEP 7 - Energy (kcal/100 g):
- Mushrooms, cooked: ~28 kcal → 57 g → 16 kcal
- Canned peaches in juice: ~60 kcal → 36 g → 22 kcal
- Strawberries: ~32 kcal → 36 g → 12 kcal
- Orange juice: ~45 kcal → 200 g → 90 kcal
- Whole milk: ~61 kcal → 200 g → 122 kcal
- Apple/pineapple juice: ~46 kcal → 200 g → 92 kcal
- Fruit yogurt: ~90 kcal → 120 g → 108 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The plate of mushrooms is a light portion (~57 g, ~16 kcal), and the beverages and yogurt drive most of the energy. Total weight ≈ 57 + 36 + 36 + 200 + 200 + 200 + 120 ≈ 849 g; total energy ≈ 16 + 22 + 12 + 90 + 122 + 92 + 108 ≈ 462 kcal. This is plausible for a full breakfast tray.
